description: Fig. 19 is a single calculated Fe–Be binary phase diagram (thermodynamic / CALPHAD equilibrium), drawn in tall-format as one panel. The ordinate is temperature T (°C) from 0 to 1800 with ticks every 200; the abscissa is Fe/(Be+Fe) (mol/mol) from 0 to 1 with ticks every 0.2, so the left edge is Be-rich and the right edge is pure Fe. A broad field labelled "Liquid" occupies the top; the liquidus dome peaks just above the 1400 °C gridline near Fe/(Be+Fe) ≈ 0.32 and descends to a minimum at ≈ 0.6 close to the 1150 °C gridline, from which a long horizontal invariant boundary runs leftwards. Three stoichiometric line compounds are drawn as single vertical lines and labelled FeBe₁₂ (≈ 0.13), FeBe₅ (≈ 0.17) and FeBe₂ (≈ 0.33); further horizontal boundaries sit near the 1150 °C, 1050 °C and 680 °C gridlines. The Be-rich (left) side shows a low-temperature HCP-A3 field and a high-temperature BCC-A2 field (roughly 1100–1300 °C); the Fe-rich (right) side is dominated by a wide BCC-A2 (ferrite) field with a narrow FCC-A1 (austenite) wedge at the extreme right edge. No numeric values are printed on the boundaries themselves.

subfigures.description: Calculated Fe–Be binary phase diagram: T (°C) 0–1800 versus Fe/(Be+Fe) (mol/mol) 0–1. Labelled fields: Liquid, BCC-A2 (both edges), HCP-A3 (Be-rich, low T), FCC-A1 (narrow wedge at the pure-Fe edge), and vertical line compounds FeBe₁₂, FeBe₅ and FeBe₂. Liquidus dome peaks just above the 1400 °C gridline near x ≈ 0.32 with a minimum near x ≈ 0.6; horizontal invariant lines near 1150, 1050 and 680 °C.

observations.observation: The figure is a single Fe–Be binary phase diagram with ordinate T (°C) from 0 to 1800 and abscissa Fe/(Be+Fe) (mol/mol) from 0 to 1; the composition axis is thus Be-rich at the left edge and pure Fe at the right edge.
A large region in the upper part of the diagram carries the printed label "Liquid".
The liquidus dome peaks just above the 1400 °C gridline at about Fe/(Be+Fe) ≈ 0.32 and falls to a minimum at about Fe/(Be+Fe) ≈ 0.6 close to the 1150 °C gridline.
Three intermetallic line compounds are drawn as single vertical lines and labelled FeBe₁₂ (≈ 0.13), FeBe₅ (≈ 0.17) and FeBe₂ (≈ 0.33) on the composition axis.
Long horizontal invariant boundaries are drawn near the 1150 °C, 1050 °C and 680 °C gridlines, running from the Be-rich left edge towards the FeBe₁₂/FeBe₅ lines.
Near the Be-rich left edge two terminal solid-solution fields are labelled: HCP-A3 at lower temperature and BCC-A2 at higher temperature (roughly 1100–1300 °C).
On the Fe-rich right side the dominant region below the liquidus is labelled BCC-A2, while a narrow wedge at the extreme right edge (Fe/(Be+Fe) → 1) is labelled FCC-A1.
No numerical composition or temperature values are printed on any phase boundary; all values are only readable against the axis ticks.
The caption states that the figure shows the relationship between composition and temperature of the Be and Fe components in thermodynamic equilibrium.
The citing text states that from the Fe–Be binary phase diagram the Be content that austenite can dissolve is <1%, and that above a certain Be content beryllium precipitates as compounds (Fig. 19).
The citing text states that beryllium in ferrite can dissolve in large quantities compared with austenite.
The citing text states that for Be elements compounds are likely formed first rather than ferrite structures.
The diagram is drawn as calculated straight-line boundaries meeting in sharp corners (equilibrium calculation output) rather than as experimentally smoothed curves with data points.

unreadable_items: Right-hand edge (Fe/(Be+Fe) ≈ 0.95–1.0): the closely spaced BCC-A2 and FCC-A1 boundary curves run together and are only partially resolvable at the supplied resolution; no invariant temperatures are labelled there
Exact temperatures of the horizontal invariant lines can only be estimated between gridlines (near 1150 °C, 1050 °C and 680 °C); no printed numeric values exist
Small rotated phase labels at the far left edge (HCP-A3, BCC-A2) are low in size and only just legible
